newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak PM says mulls simpler bankruptcies.
newsitem.headline: Slovak PM says mulls simpler bankruptcies.

text.p: Slovak Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar said on Friday the government was considering simplifying the process of bankruptcy for firms considered incapable of survival.
"The government is very much considering...opening the door to the bankruptcy law in the sense of shortening and simplifying the whole process," Meciar said in a regular radio adddress.
"The elimination of indebtedness will be done based on a decision that the companies which are able to survive with the banking system and government's support will continue," he said.
He did not specify who would make the decision.
"For those which are determined to be not (capable), the debtor can be put into bankruptcy or offer a settlement (for its debts)," Meciar said.
Despite a big problem of inter-company debt, companies rarely declare bankruptcy in Slovakia.
As of January 1, the economy ministry said 79 state companies with total assets of 15 billion crowns were going through the liquidation process.
Last September, the Slovak parliament approved an amendemt to the bankruptcy law preventing state firms and those officially classed as strategic from going under.
Strategic firms included enterprises such as telecoms company Slovenske Telekomunikace, energy monopoly Slovenske Elektrarne, oil refiner Slovnaft and steel producer VSZ.
It was not clear whether Meciar intended that these strategic firms could also be made bankrupt.
